title: Goose v2 Skin
eyebrow: Build plan for approval · Models issue #18, one fused skin and a neck root that forks into three · nothing changed yet
approval: Build plan approved: goose v2 skin

short.lead: This is the first step of the goose version 2 model (issue #17), and the step that unblocks #19, #20 and #21. Today the goose is 1,072 separate pieces, with each neck, wing and leg pushed into an egg-shaped body. I built a quick throwaway test that melts the soft parts into one closed skin and gives the neck a single root that forks into three. It ran in 5 seconds, with no holes in the surface. The pictures below come from that test, untextured. Three choices decide how the real build does it.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it does and what it needs from you.
items: bulb
Neck root
One root rising from the chest that forks into three

The main neck and the two side necks start from one thick root, about 1.5 m wide at the chest, that splits into three just above the breast. The three heads stay exactly where version 1 has them, so the height stays 6.75 m and the rig in #21 only has to move the neck bones.
Your answer to the question on fork height.

items.alt: Untextured test render of a single thick neck root splitting into three necks above a smooth body
items.caption: The throwaway test: one root, forking at about 3.05 m.

items: hammer
Fused skin
Melt the soft parts into one closed skin

The body, the three necks, both wing arms and both legs are merged into one surface. Each join is then smoothed into a wide curve, about 0.3 m across, so the body flows into the neck instead of meeting it at an edge. The tail end of the body is already part of the body tube, so it joins automatically. The hard details stay their own pieces: the teeth, ribs, claws, crowns, feathers, toes and scale rings, and the heads.
Your answer to the question on method.

items.caption: The throwaway test at the wing root: no seam line.

items: check
Checks
Add a one-shell check to the validator

The existing checks still run on the new model: triangle budget, height, nothing below the floor and every piece closed. A new check counts the soft skin's separate pieces and refuses to export unless it is exactly one. The skin is capped at 75,000 triangles. The soft parts use 62,452 today, so the whole model lands near 285,000 of the 300,000 budget, which leaves #19 about 15,000 triangles. #19 can trim elsewhere if it needs more.
Nothing from you.
eye

choices: method
How should the soft parts be fused?
A
Melt them together, then smooth the joins

Rebuild the soft parts as one surface on a fine 2.2 cm grid, then smooth only the vertices within 0.3 m of a join. This is what the test did: the surface came out closed in both test runs, and the join width is one number.

choices.alt: Untextured test render of three necks fused smoothly into the body
choices.caption: Method A on today's three necks.

choices: B
Cut and stitch the original surfaces

Keep each part's original surface and cut and stitch them where they cross. This keeps the version 1 surface layout away from the joins. With eight tubes it fails easily, and a stitched crease needs extra work to look like muscle.

I suggest option A (melt and smooth). The test already passed the closed-surface check, and #20 re-bakes the textures across the whole skin anyway, so losing the original surface layout costs nothing.
fork
Where should the neck root split into three?
A
Just above the breast, at about 3.05 m
A short, massive root. The side necks stay long enough to swing their heads in the attack clips.

choices.alt: Untextured test render of the whole goose with the neck forking low
choices.caption: The test with the fork at about 3.05 m.

choices: B
Halfway up, at about 3.5 m
A taller trunk, closer to how a hydra is drawn. The side heads sit at 4.05 m, so each side neck would be only about 0.55 m long, which would look stubby and limit their swing.
I suggest option A (just above the breast), because the side heads are only 4.05 m up.
texture
How should goose_v2 be textured until #20 is done?
A
Carry version 1's colours over as a stand-in

Each point of the new skin takes its colour and pattern from the nearest version 1 surface, baked into art/goose/textures_v2/. It looks like today's goose, with soft colour changes at the joins, and #20 replaces it.
B
Leave it untextured until #20
Faster, and nothing is baked twice. The review sheet then shows a grey model next to the concept.
I suggest option A (carry the colours over), because #18 asks for a review sheet beside the concept, and a grey model is hard to judge against it.
